issues.claim: R3-21's END for V09 §4.2 (l. 1652–1653) makes the working-layer switch write the document: 'Switching layer also sets the layer's visibility on (§7.8's layer controls: `LayerSpec.visible`, written by `setLayer`, §8.4)'. `setLayer` is a logged, undoable style event (§7.4). Find's Go there works through that switch: V09 §4.21.10 (8) (l. 3514–3516: 'Below sets the working layer to Below …; Sky sets it to Sky, … and a hidden sky layer visible'); V05 §5.6 (3) (l. 2319: 'Go there turns its visibility on, as switching the working layer does'); T-V9-83 (g) ('a hidden sky layer shown'). The underground is hidden by default at every rung (II.7.1, D-3), so the common case, Go there on a Below match, now appends a `setLayer` to the edit log. This contradicts owner item 120 (a) ('Find never changes the model, the document, its hash or the edit log'), §9.5's Find ('It sends no event and changes no … log … Go there sets the working layer and band — view changes'), V09 §4.21.10 (1) and V04 §5.1 ('a view key, never an edit'). T-V9-83 (g) and (i) ('the log unchanged by Find') cannot both pass. A viewer may never edit (§11.3 Roles; §11.2 `edit` is an editing role's call), so a viewer's working-layer switch, or Go there to a hidden layer, needs an event its role cannot send, and no outcome is defined. Before this round V09 called the visibility 'view state only', and the paths did not meet. Grade: an owner rule contradicted where a builder following V09 and V05 would implement it, on a common path; at the least MAJOR (a bar that cannot pass).
issues.required_change: Keep visibility as document style state, written only by a deliberate T12 `dress` toggle (R3-21); neither Find nor a viewer writes it. (1) V09 §4.2: 'Switching layer also sets the layer's visibility on (§7.8's layer controls: `LayerSpec.visible`, written by `setLayer`, §8.4) and dims the other layers to 35 % opacity.' → 'Switching layer dims the other layers to 35 % opacity and writes nothing to the document. A layer whose `LayerSpec.visible` is false (§8.4: document style state, written only by T12 `dress`'s logged `setLayer`) stays hidden, and the switch shows `info.layer.hidden` ("{layer} is hidden on this map."). For a role that may write style (owner, editor; §11.3), it also offers **Show it** — T12 `dress`'s toggle, `setLayer { layer, spec: { visible: true } }`, its own undo step. A viewer gets no **Show it**.' (2) V09 §4.21.10 (8): 'Sky sets it to Sky, the island menu's `key` to the match's island and a hidden sky layer visible (V05 §5.6 (3))' → 'Sky sets it to Sky and the island menu's `key` to the match's island — view keys only, never a `setLayer` (item 120 (a)). On a hidden layer the flight lands on its ghost pins with V09 §4.2's `info.layer.hidden` and its **Show it**, which is T12 `dress`'s edit, not Find's.' (3) V09 §3.16 row 21's outcome 'switching the working layer turns its visibility on (by `setLayer`, §8.4)' → 'the layer stays hidden, with `info.layer.hidden` and, for an owner or editor, **Show it** (a logged `setLayer`); a viewer's switch writes nothing'. (4) T-V9-83 (g): '(a hidden sky layer shown)' → '(on a hidden layer `info.layer.hidden`, no event logged)'; (i) stands. (5) V09 §4.9 adds the row `info.layer.hidden`. (6) END at V05 §5.6 (3): 'and Go there turns its visibility on, as switching the working layer does' → 'and Go there leaves its visibility as it stands (V09 §4.2: visibility is document style, which only T12 `dress`'s `setLayer` writes), the flight landing on its ghost pins'.

issues.claim: R3-16 (e) rules that at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE `info.crisis.ruinedFor` is the village `WhyProvider`'s answer row, shown once. V09 §4.21.12 (4) and §5.8 now show it only from that provider. V07 §4.5 and W74 say the provider reads '§2.9's `crises` and `week` with DR44 at the viewer's key … never from the model'; its `info.village.season` and `info.village.festival` rows are likewise 'read from view state'. No interface carries a view into a why answer: §11.2's `why` member is `{ kind: 'why'; id; path?; mode?; historyPage? }`; V10 §2.13's `WhyProvider.explain(model, id, path, key, { mode, historyPage })` takes none; V10 §3.9 calls providers 'over the committed model with the caller's key'; V09's `WhyCardModel` reads `query({ kind: 'why' })` with no view; and J-V10.125 says 'a `why` section is model-side and cannot know the view's week'. These three rows' inputs have no producer (principle (7)). One builder adds a view parameter; another, following V10, cannot produce the rows, and the village card shows no crisis line — the case R3-16 (e) meant to settle.
issues.required_change: One view-bound why at the API's home. (1) §11.2's `why` member: `{ kind: 'why'; id: Id; path?: string; mode?: 'asPlaced'|'asNow'; historyPage?: number; view?: ViewHandle /* a view-bound why: a provider whose rows state a view's look — V07 §4.5's crisis, season and festival rows — reads that view's §2.9 week, yearWeek, festival and crises and its looks evaluation (LooksAnswer) at the view's effective key; absent, no such row is given */ }`; *Knowledge* adds 'a `why` with a `view` admits its view-bound rows as `looks` does'. (2) END at V10: §2.13's `WhyProvider.explain` opts gain `view?: { week: number; yearWeek: number; festival: ViewState['festival']; crises: ViewState['crises']; looks: LooksAnswer }`; §3.9's query paragraph adds 'and, for a view-bound why, the view's state and `looks` answer'; the `why` tool passes `ClerkSession.view` where present (§3.5). (3) END at V09: §2.7's `WhyCardModel` reads `query({ kind: 'why', …, view })` with the card's view. (4) END at V07: §4.5 and W74 cite `opts.view` for the three rows.

issues.claim: V09's crisis card, why lines, legend entries and Find list read §11.2's `looks` reader, 'the one evaluation `live.crises` draws'. §8.2 re-runs that evaluation 'when the week crosses a condition's edge …, the crisis display or the key changes, the model the view draws changes (a commit, or the week crossing to another frame)'. V09 §2.12's rows re-read it on fewer triggers: l. 1005 (card and lines) 'rebuilt at each week change, absorb and `onEffectiveKey`' — no `crises` change, no commit; l. 1008 (damage lines, whose plan-panel look lines read the look's `districts` and `lookLevel`) — no `crises` change. Two normal paths diverge. Preview a crisis, or Show crises off, changes `crises`: the map draws the new looks while the card, Find's list and the plan panel keep the old ones, though V09 §4.21.12 (2) and (4) promise the preview's line. A commit that splits or merges a struck district changes a disaster's units 'at that commit' (V01 §3.16): the map draws the new districts while the card's `facts` row and the plan panel's look lines keep the old list until the next week change. One builder follows the row, another §8.2.
issues.required_change: V09 §2.12 l. 1005: 'rebuilt at each week change, absorb and `onEffectiveKey`' → 're-read whenever the evaluation §8.2's `live.crises` runs changes: each change of §2.9's `week` or `crises` (**Show crises**, **Preview a crisis**), each `doc.changed` (a commit, an absorb, an undo or redo, a regenerate — an edit that splits or merges a struck district changes a disaster's units at that commit, V01 §3.16) and each `onEffectiveKey`'. l. 1008 adds '; for the plan panel's look lines, at each re-read of §11.2's `looks` reader (the row above)'. T-V9-85 adds: a preview picked and the switch turned off with the card open each update the card and Find's list at once, and a district split on a dossier fixture with a disaster standing updates the card's `facts` row at that commit.

issues.claim: T-ER-21's outcome for the host's commands (l. 16624) reads 'the week and the selection view state that travels, the layers a logged `setLayer` — never an input', in the words adjudication-r3's note gives. §11.3, the home, says the selection is not view state: `view.set { select: ids }` selects as a user's list pick would and reports `entity.selected` — 'a command, never a stored key' — so it neither persists nor travels as `view.changed`. The bar's own fixture (byte-identical replay without the host) passes either way. A test writer checking the stated outcome would look for a travelling selection the bridge never sends.
issues.required_change: T-ER-21's outcome: 'the week and the selection view state that travels, the layers a logged `setLayer` — never an input' → 'the week view state that travels, the selection a command (the frame selects and reports `entity.selected`; never a stored key), the layers a logged `setLayer` — never an input'.

issues.claim: V10 §3.23 row 26 (l. 2678) gives 'a layer off' the outcome 'layer visibility is view state and never filters a read, which admits by key'. By R3-21 (a), §8.4 and §7.4, layer visibility is `LayerSpec.visible`, the document's style state, written by a logged `setLayer`, the very event V10's own §4.1 T12 encoder writes (`setLayer { layer, spec: { visible } }`). The outcome that counts — a hidden layer never filters a read — is the same; the classification is the retired one.
issues.required_change: V10 §3.23 row 26: 'layer visibility is view state and never filters a read, which admits by key' → 'layer visibility (`LayerSpec.visible`, the document's style state, written by a logged `setLayer`, §8.4) never filters a read, which admits by key'.

issues.claim: R3-02 (principle (5)) keeps review-process ids out of design text, and VAT-r2-06's fix removed every `R2-nn` from V09. Assemble-r3's census (section 8) leaves four canon conflict and agreement ids in V09's design text for the verifiers: l. 598 '(V09-XAGREE-1)', l. 2120 '(V06-AGREE-1)', l. 3283 '(V09-ICONF-4's rule)', l. 3844 '(V09-ICONF-4)'. Each stands beside its design home, which already gives the rule. The base's six sites of the class are VDC3-08. No rule changes.
